title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment.
abstract: Agentic systems — large language model (LLM)-based architectures capable of reasoning, planning, acting, and coordinating with tools and other agents — are rapidly transitioning from research prototypes to production-scale deployments across domains such as software engineering, scientific discovery, and finance. While academic work has emphasized benchmarks and algorithmic innovation, deployment raises new challenges around robustness, safety, and reliability. This tutorial brings together researchers and practitioners to explore advances in reasoning and planning, multi-agent coordination, and evaluation, highlighting open challenges arising from deployment experience. Through applied case studies in pharmaceutical discovery and financial systems, we analyze common design patterns that make agentic systems successful, and discuss practical mitigation strategies for failure modes, such as verification pipelines, fallback mechanisms, and human-in-the-loop supervision. Attendees will gain a comprehensive view of the field along with concrete design patterns, evaluation checklists, and templates for safe and reliable deployment across industries.

title: The KDD 2026 Panel Beyond Scaling - What Will Define the Next Decade of AI? New Frontiers in Knowledge Discovery from Data.
abstract: Over the past decade, the rapid scaling of data, compute, and model size has driven remarkable advances in artificial intelligence. From foundation models to generative AI, scaling has emerged as a dominant paradigm for progress. Yet, important limitations are becoming increasingly evident, including challenges in extrapolation, reliability, efficiency, evaluation, and real-world deployment. This panel will examine what comes next. If scaling alone is not sufficient, what new paradigms, system-level advances, and interdisciplinary approaches will define the next decade of AI? The discussion will explore emerging directions such as reasoning and agentic systems, as well as hybrid approaches that integrate learning with structure, prior knowledge, or explicit models of the world. It will also consider the growing importance of evaluation, trust, and deployment in real-world settings, and how these factors may influence the transition from predictive performance towards deeper forms of knowledge discovery from data, including applications in scientific discovery and other high-impact domains. Bringing together perspectives from academia, industry, and domain sciences, the panel will reflect on the evolving foundations of AI and outline key opportunities and challenges for the KDD community as it navigates this next phase of the field.

title: The Second Workshop on SciSoc Agents & LLMs: Agentic AI for Scientific and Societal Advances.
abstract: The Second Workshop on SciSoc Agents & LLMs: Agentic AI for Scientific and Societal Advances aims to explore the emerging paradigm of agentic artificial intelligence, where Large Language Models (LLMs) are combined with autonomous agents, tools, memory, and multi-step reasoning to drive scientific discovery and address critical societal challenges. As LLMs continue to advance in capability, their integration into agent-based systems enables more interactive, goal-driven, and adaptive workflows that go beyond passive text generation. In particular, Agentic AI systems have demonstrated strong potential in orchestrating complex scientific pipelines, reasoning over large and heterogeneous datasets, interacting with external environments, and supporting decision-making in domains such as healthcare, environmental science, education, public policy, and social sciences. By bringing together researchers and practitioners from AI, data mining, science, and society, this workshop aims to foster a comprehensive understanding of how LLMs and agent-based architectures jointly redefine traditional research methodologies. Participants will explore novel agentic frameworks, multi-agent collaboration, and real-world deployments that leverage LLM-powered agents to accelerate scientific progress and generate meaningful societal impact.
